    On this site · Live tournament preparation

    From the first seat to the end of the day.

    Prepare for breaks, table moves, bagging chips and finishing a tournament day without treating each logistical step as a strategic problem.

    Read matching section

    Searchable article text, without exercise answers

    A tournament day includes small logistical decisions that rarely make the highlight reel. Know what to check when the table changes, when a break ends and when staff announce the end of a playing day.

    Before entering, check the possible continuation schedule and your route home. Pack only what the venue permits and what you will use: required identification, a layer for comfort, and appropriate food or water if allowed. Plan around the event rather than assuming a convenient break or early finish will appear. Locate the official tournament clock and know where to ask a procedural question. Confirm the current blinds and ante before play rather than relying on an old photograph of the display.

    At a break, confirm the announced restart time. Treat that time as the end of the break, not the moment to join a food queue. Allow room to return to the correct table and settle in without rushing. Leaving a seat is not necessarily a pause in its forced costs: TDA procedures address absent players and the posting of blinds and antes. Ask staff what applies rather than assuming your stack is protected while you are away. Use a break for something restorative before turning it into another work session. A short private note about a completed hand can wait until you are away from play and the event permits it. No hand is worth delaying the game to document.

    Confirm the destination table and seat, and follow staff instructions for moving your chips. Ask about the approved carrying method rather than pocketing chips or improvising. At the destination, verify that you are in the intended place and clarify the next blind obligation with the dealer. Check the denominations at the new table rather than estimating value from pile height. A new seat and new opponents also mean that an earlier hand note should not silently inherit the new table's positions or stacks.

    If staff end the day with players returning later, follow their counting, recording and bagging instructions. Confirm the recorded total and the required identifying information before finishing. Check the restart date, time and location directly with the organizer. Keep your private record of the count and restart details. Do not publish a bag label or receipt containing a name, barcode or other identifier. An account can simply say what the verified chip count represents without showing the document. Whether that stage also earns a payout depends on the event. Do not infer “in the money” from a bag, a surviving stack or the words “Day 2.” The tournament-progression guide separates stage changes from prize eligibility.

    Confirm any required organizer steps, collect your belongings and record the actual costs and return. A receipt is more useful than an estimate when the exact figure is available. Keep an unresolved payment question for the organizer rather than declaring it settled in a public post. For study, save one question and the facts needed to revisit it. Do not force a complete strategic explanation immediately after elimination. The hand-note guide distinguishes a quick factual record from a later analysis. For a compact version, use the event and day planner . You do not need to complete every field to benefit from checking the few details that matter to your outing.

    On this site · Live tournament preparation

    Keep a hand note you can actually review.

    Capture positions, stacks, actions and uncertainty after play, with a checked fictional pot ledger and a reusable private note template.

    Read matching section

    Searchable article text, without exercise answers

    “Lost with ace-queen” records a result, not a reviewable hand. A useful note preserves who could act, the amounts involved and the moment you want to revisit. It can be short without pretending to be complete.

    Use the record after the hand and only where the organizer allows it. The safest default is to wait until you are away from the table and active play. TDA rules restrict device use with a live hand and strategy tools at the table. A note template is not an exception to those rules. Do not record covertly, slow the game to write or assume a filming permission includes unrestricted recording. A missing detail can remain missing.

    Record the game and stage, blinds and ante, number of players, positions and relevant starting stacks. Keep your cards and the board in street order. Then list each action with its amount, including checks and folds that explain who remained in the hand. Write raises to 2,200 when 2,200 is the new total for that street. Write adds 1,200 to call when that is the extra amount paid. “Raises 2,200” can leave the reader unsure which you meant. For unfamiliar notation, use words instead of compact symbols. Mark an estimate where it appears: “about 28,000 before forced bets,” “turn suit unknown,” or “reconstructed from memory after the session.” Do not reserve uncertainty for a general disclaimer at the bottom.

    Illustration only, not one of Nolan's hands Eight-handed no-limit hold'em. Blinds 500/1,000; a 1,000 big blind ante. Button has 32,000 and big blind 28,000 before forced bets. Button holds ace of spades, queen of clubs. Everyone folds to the button, who raises to 2,200. Small blind folds; big blind adds 1,200 to call. Flop: ace of hearts, seven of diamonds, two of clubs. Big blind checks; button bets 1,800; big blind folds. The preflop pot is 500 + 1,000 + 1,000 + 2,200 + 1,200 = 5,900 . The small blind, big blind, big blind ante, button's raise and additional call are separate contributions. The uncalled 1,800 is returned; the contested pot is 5,900 . The button's net chip gain is 3,700 , not 5,900 or 7,700. The note does not establish the opponent's cards or whether the flop bet was the best action. A useful review question could be: “Which worse hands could continue against this size, under a stated range assumption?” That question belongs after the record, not inside it as an observed fact.

    If the ante is unknown, do not publish an exact starting pot as though it were recorded. If a suit is uncertain, do not assign a specific blocker. When only a range of stack sizes is plausible, either keep the analysis conditional or choose a different hand for an exact worked example. Check that the pot ledger and final stacks agree with the described payments and refunds. Keep both chips and big blinds where helpful, but name the blind level used. The pot-odds workshop handles the extra amount required to call; the review guide takes the next step into interpretation.

    Use position labels rather than names. Remove ticket numbers, faces and identifying details that are unnecessary to understand the decision. Keep remembered thoughts separate from later analysis, and obtain appropriate permission for any material involving others. The blank hand-capture sheet is available to copy, print or download. Complete it privately. There is no upload field and the website does not receive your answers.

    On this site · Results and review

    Choose a study tool by the question it answers.

    Match a study question to free lessons, equity tools or solver documentation. Compare fit, first steps, limits and access without unsupported product rankings.

    Read matching section

    Searchable article text, without exercise answers

    An equity calculator, a solver and a trainer can all display impressive numbers while answering different questions. Start with the question you need to answer, not the product with the most features.

    Equity calculator: how often do these hands or ranges win at showdown? You supply cards, ranges and any known board. The result describes showdown equity for those inputs, not automatically the value of calling when later betting remains. Equilab's official introduction is one example of this category. An opponent's entered range is still your assumption. ICM calculator: how does this payout model value the stacks? An ICM calculation uses the remaining stacks and payouts to estimate prize equity under its model. It is not a cash-out offer or, by itself, a full strategy for the next hand. See ICMIZER's model explanation and this site's worked tournament-equity guide . Solver: what strategies does a specified game model produce? A solver works within the configured game, including allowed actions, sizes, ranges and objective. A well-computed result for the wrong situation can still be the wrong reference. The PioSOLVER documentation and HoldemResources documentation provide official starting points for understanding setup rather than only looking at the output. Solution library: which previously calculated spot am I looking at? A stored solution saves setup work but still needs to match the hand. Check the format, positions, stack depth, ante and action sequence. GTO Wizard's official product overview distinguishes pre-solved material from custom solving. Availability within a particular subscription needs to be checked with the provider. Trainer: can I practice against this reference? A trainer compares choices with its reference. Treat the score as feedback within that exercise, not independent proof of broad poker ability. Before drilling, learn which game and solution the exercise uses and how errors are scored.

    For an unclear call price, a pot ledger and ordinary arithmetic may be enough. For a question about showdown equity, compare clearly specified ranges. For a payout question, inspect the stacks and prizes before asking a tournament model. For strategic comparisons across future actions, read the model's setup requirements first. When the uncertainty is “I do not know the opponent's range,” a more expensive subscription does not make that range observed. Try explicit alternative assumptions rather than reporting one output as the truth.

    Start with the unresolved question, then open the matching shortlist. Access labels describe the linked destination: a free manual does not make its associated software free. These selections reflect public-page scope, not hands-on product testing or performance rankings. For a completed cash hand, use the five-session cash-game route and its blank worksheet. A pot ledger may answer the question without any software.

    Identify one repeatable study task and confirm that the product supports its exact game, operating system and required features. Check the provider's current access limits, renewal terms, cancellation process and trial conditions. Do not rely on prices or feature claims copied into an old comparison article. Try a small example whose arithmetic you can check. Learn what you can save or export and whether an explanation remains understandable without a screenshot of colored cells. Choose no subscription when the documentation or existing free exercises already meet the need.

    Record the starting pot, stacks, ranges, available actions, payouts where relevant, and any convergence or approximation information the product supplies. GTO Wizard's explanation of solvers discusses why the game tree is a modeling choice. A displayed decimal does not eliminate a mismatched input or an omitted action. This guide now includes task-based shortlists, not a hands-on product test or an accuracy certification. Public documentation was read for scope; paid software and calculation quality were not independently tested for this article. The software directory keeps provider links and access labels together.

    PokerStars Live's published rules prohibit strategy software, charts and qualifying AI assistance at the table, including assistance relayed by spectators. Other operators have their own restrictions. Use these resources after play and check the actual operator's current policy. Complete one resource-check sheet : the question, inputs, answer, remaining uncertainty and next step. A reproducible small study is more useful than collecting tools you cannot yet explain.

    On this site · Results and review

    Read poker advice without borrowing its certainty.

    Evaluate a video, chart, article or forum answer by its question, evidence and assumptions, then turn it into one checkable study task.

    Read matching section

    Searchable article text, without exercise answers

    A clear explanation can still leave out the condition that makes it useful. Before adopting a rule from a video, chart or discussion, work out what it actually claims and whether the situation matches yours.

    Replace “this is how professionals play” with something narrower: “What is the claimed response at this position, stack depth and action sequence?” Distinguish a definition, a calculation, a strategic opinion, a personal account and a product claim. They need different checks. A rules question belongs with the event's current official rules and staff. A product-feature question belongs with current provider documentation. A personal story can be valuable without becoming a general recommendation.

    Check the game, number of players, positions, stack convention, ante, action history and objective. Is the chart for an unopened pot or for facing a raise? Does it allow calls and small raises, or only push and fold? Does “20 BB” describe stacks before posting, chips remaining, or something else? A heads-up reference is not automatically a six-player reference. The short-stack input guide explains these compatibility checks. For a solver screenshot, the provider's explanation of game-tree inputs is a useful reminder that the visible answer is only part of the model.

    When watching a hand, note which cards the player knew then and which cards the audience sees later. A revealed bluff can explain the outcome without proving that the call was justified beforehand. A selected tournament story also does not contain every entry cost or all of a player's results. Pause before the reveal and write one reason for each plausible action. Then ask what the outcome actually teaches. The river Decision Lab provides a fictional exercise in keeping the same decision record through two different endings.

    A fictional disagreement worth inspecting Two explanations give different answers for an apparently similar 20 BB spot. One assumes an unopened pot in chip EV.     You win a hand when every other player folds, or by having the strongest five-card hand among players who reach the showdown. A tied best hand can share the pot. You do not have to bet on every turn to keep playing; the guided hand below explains the actions. A standard deck has 52 different cards: thirteen ranks in each of four suits. The usual high-to-low rank order is A K Q J T 9 8 7 6 5 4 3 2 . A is ace, K king, Q queen, J jack and T ten. The four suits are spades ♠, hearts ♥, diamonds ♦ and clubs ♣. Suits do not outrank one another. You receive two private cards . The shared board arrives as three cards on the flop, one on the turn, then one on the river. Once all five shared cards are out, choose the strongest five from your seven available cards. Use zero, one or two private cards. An ace can be low in A-2-3-4-5, but a straight cannot wrap through K-A-2-3-4. Ready for the course? Begin lesson 1 after these basics and the worked selection below.     On this site · Cash-game study

    Study cash games without importing tournament assumptions.

    Separate cash-game costs, effective stacks and multiway decisions from tournament models, with a worked rake example.

    Read matching section

    Searchable article text, without exercise answers

    The same ace-queen hand can sit inside very different problems. A cash-game hand has a cash ledger and a house-charge structure. A tournament hand may also involve changing blinds and a payout model. Start by naming the actual game instead of borrowing a chart from the other format. For callers, action order and separate pots, use the multiway-pot workshop .

    Record the stakes, game, number of players, positions, effective stacks, antes or straddles and the exact action. A fictional 300-chip stack with a 3-chip big blind is 100 BB, but that alone does not tell you which ranges, bet sizes or fees a reference assumed. In an ordinary cash game, chips have a fixed redemption value. That is not a guarantee of profit, and it does not make every pot a simple heads-up calculation. The position and stack guide explains the units; the tournament-equity guide shows why prize value is a different objective.

    Read the actual room or operator's fee schedule. PokerStars' official rake page below illustrates how an operator documents rates and caps; it does not supply the rates for a live cardroom. Percentage rake, fixed collection, promotional drops and time charges should not be silently treated as the same cost. Fictional river example, not a recommended wager The pot is 80 before an opponent bets 40. You face a 40 call, with no later betting. Before charges, the final pot would be 160. Suppose this invented game charges 5% of that pot, capped at 6, with no other deductions. The charge is 6 , leaving 154 to award. The break-even equity is 40 / 154 = about 25.97% , not 40 / 160 = 25%. At exactly 25% equity, the call's expected value relative to folding is 0.25 × 154 - 40 = -1.50 . With no charge it would be zero. These are conditional calculations, not an estimate of your actual equity. Count a charge only once. If a displayed pot already excludes a collection, do not subtract it again. If a fee has already been paid regardless of the current decision, separate that sunk cost from additional costs caused by calling. The example assumes the stated charge is taken from the final pot after a call.

    Before applying a heads-up lesson to a multiway hand, write who can still act after you. A call may not close the betting. Another player may raise, a short stack may have a separate main pot, and not everyone is eligible for every chip. The side-pot lab lets you check that bookkeeping without guessing strategy. When several players call a raise, the limped and multiway guide shows how to rebuild action order, stacks and ranges before choosing a bet. Do not turn a convenient simplification into an observed fact. “Assume the third player folds” is a scenario to test, not a description of a hand in which that player has not acted. A chart with two participants cannot establish the effects of a third participant's decisions.

    The implied-odds article below introduces future payments after a draw completes. When reviewing its logic, ask whether the opponent would actually continue, whether the draw can make a second-best hand, and how much is available to win. A large opposing stack does not mean that stack will be paid to you. Start with the amount required now, then write separate future branches. In one branch the draw misses; in another it completes and receives no further payment; in another it gets action. Naming these branches is more useful than adding an optimistic future amount to every outcome.

    SplitSuit and The Poker Bank provide different entry points into cash-game teaching. The Crush Live Poker video catalogue adds live-hand material with its own access conditions. Choose a question such as bet sizing or effective stacks, then compare the assumptions instead of trying to finish every archive. Record actual buy-ins, top-ups and cash-outs separately from your hand-review conclusions. An attractive hourly result over a short sample is not a demonstrated long-run win rate. Choose personal time and spending limits without relying on predicted winnings. Study does not require paying for another playing session.

    Omaha, lowball and mixed games: know which rules changed.

    Compare hand construction, low qualifiers and game rotations, then work through an Omaha hi-lo split-pot example.

    Searchable article text, without exercise answers

    Learning another poker game starts with three questions: which cards may I use, what hand wins, and how is the pot divided? Answer those before transferring a familiar hold'em lesson. Continue with the Omaha hi-lo workshop for quartering and counterfeiting, or the stud and lowball workshop for hand comparisons.

    Starting distinctions, with full rules linked below Game Cards used at showdown What wins? Hold'em Best five from the board and two hole cards; zero, one or two hole cards may play. High hand. Omaha high Exactly two hole cards and three board cards. High hand; having more hole cards does not change the two-card rule. Omaha hi-lo Exactly two plus three for each half, possibly different combinations. High and qualifying eight-or-better low share the pot. Stud high / stud hi-lo Best five from an individual's seven cards, not an Omaha board. High only, or high and qualifying low, depending on the game. Razz Best five-card low from an individual's seven. Ace-to-five low, without an eight-or-better qualifier. 2-7 triple draw Five-card hand after up to three draws. Deuce-to-seven low; aces are high and straights and flushes count against you. Badugi Up to four cards with distinct ranks and suits. A qualifying four-card hand beats a three-card hand; then compare low ranks. Use the Omaha , razz and selected rule references below for the full procedures. A mix such as HORSE or eight-game is a rotation, not one blended set of hand rankings.

    In a fictional Omaha hand, you hold ace of spades, king of diamonds, queen of clubs and jack of hearts. The board is two of spades, seven of spades, nine of spades, jack of spades and three of diamonds. You do not have a flush: using four board spades and one hole spade is illegal in Omaha. Only one of your hole cards is a spade. Five-card Omaha adds a hole card, not permission to use three. Do not use a hold'em hand evaluator, or a four-card range table, without checking which game it supports. A visually impressive screenshot is not enough to establish a legal hand.

    A fictional Omaha eight-or-better showdown Board: three of clubs, four of diamonds, eight of hearts, king of spades, king of diamonds. Player A: ace of spades, two of spades, king of clubs, queen of hearts. Player B: ace of hearts, two of hearts, queen of clubs, jack of diamonds. For high, A uses king of clubs and queen of hearts with the two board kings and eight: three kings . B cannot beat that. For low, both use ace-two with the board's three-four-eight: 8-4-3-2-A . With a 200-chip pot to distribute after any applicable charges, A wins the 100-chip high half and 50 of the tied low half, receiving 150 . B receives 50 . B has been quartered. These are awards, not each player's net profit; their earlier contributions are not specified. A low needs five different qualifying ranks. Having ace-two does not guarantee a qualifying low on every board, and two players can hold equally good lows. When no one qualifies in this format, the high winner receives the whole pot. Those rules do not mean that all lowball games have a qualifier.

    In ace-to-five lowball, aces are low and straights and flushes do not spoil the low. In deuce-to-seven, aces are high and straights and flushes count against it. Thus an unsuited 7-5-4-3-2 is an excellent deuce-to-seven hand, while A-2-3-4-5 is not the lowball winner it would be under ace-to-five rules. Badugi adds another distinction: rank and suit duplication can reduce the number of cards that count. Read its four-card ranking rule before comparing the numerical height of two hands.

    In mixed games, confirm the rotation and betting structure before applying an action rule. A fixed-limit round and a pot-limit round do not offer the same raise sizes. In short-deck hold'em, even the familiar high-hand hierarchy can change: the linked PokerStars six-plus rules rank a flush over a full house. Other organizers' short-deck rules need their own check.

    These are introductions and rule references, not recommended ranges or evidence that a particular game is currently offered at a venue. Prepared with AI assistance. Published October 8, 2026 .     On this site · Learning resources

    Choose a poker book or course you will actually use.

    Match prerequisites, format and one study goal before buying; distinguish author descriptions, independent reviews and free course material.

    Read matching section

    Searchable article text, without exercise answers

    A useful poker book is one you can work with, not just one that appears on a “best books” list. Match the subject and prerequisites to a specific question, then decide whether the format will help you practice. Prefer audio or video? The media study guide separates inspected transcripts, transcript interfaces and show notes.

    For rules and hand construction, begin with the free learning path . For tournament logistics, use the field guide . A dense game-theory book is an inefficient way to answer “how do I register?” and a basic rules guide will not explain a solver's convergence. Write a narrower objective: understand bluffing incentives, reconstruct a pot, compare range assumptions, or recognize a payout effect. Then inspect the table of contents, prerequisites and a legally available sample. A title containing “modern” or “advanced” is not evidence that its examples match your situation.

    Play Optimal Poker is presented by Andrew Brokos as an introduction to game-theoretic reasoning applied to poker. Modern Poker Theory is presented by D&B Poker as Michael Acevedo's software-informed no-limit hold'em treatment. Those are descriptions of scope from the author or publisher, not claims that this site has read and tested the full books. The linked Mathematics of Poker review serves a different purpose. Brokos discusses the demands of following mathematical arguments and translating simplified games into poker. It is his signed assessment of Chen and Ankenman's book, not the book itself and not our independent evaluation of every chapter. MIT's two archived courses offer free lecture material. The 2015 course includes analytical teaching, while the 2016 course provides an introduction through video lectures. They are historical courses with their own scope, not continuously updated instructions for current software. Use the original course pages to inspect what is actually available.

    Check the game and format, the assumed mathematical background, the kind of worked exercises, the date or edition, and the access conditions. For a subscription, confirm renewal and cancellation terms. For videos, check whether usable captions, transcripts or downloadable notes exist rather than assuming that a “course” includes them. A publisher's sample tells you more about the writing than a testimonial. A review can reveal a mismatch that a product page does not emphasize. Neither replaces trying a small, legal sample yourself. No purchase is necessary when free material already answers your question.

    Before reading, write a question. During reading, copy the important inputs in your own words: positions, stacks, pot size, available actions and the opponent assumptions. After reading, close the chapter and reconstruct the example. Then change one input and ask which parts of the conclusion still follow. For example, a calculation might assume that calling ends the betting. Change the example so another player can raise. The original arithmetic may remain correct inside its model while no longer resolving the new decision. That is a useful learning result, not a failure to memorize the author. Keep direct quotations short and attributed. Do not copy copyrighted books, course downloads or paywalled charts into public notes or a hand review. A link to an authorized sample is different from redistributing a pirated file.

    After a few lessons, ask whether you can explain something more clearly, reproduce a calculation, or identify a missing assumption. Subscription time and pages read are activity measures, not proof of strategic improvement. A tournament cash immediately after reading is not evidence that the book caused it. Use the advice-reading guide when two authors disagree. For a tool rather than a course, use the software-category guide . Keep one next step, not a queue of purchases.

    No ranked winner is implied. Public descriptions and the review were inspected; the complete paid books and courses were not independently tested. Prepared with AI assistance.     On this site · Poker research

    A map of poker research, without the inflated claims.

    Find original research on regret, sampling, poker AI and evaluation, with explicit boundaries between game-solving results and playing strength.

    Read matching section

    Searchable article text, without exercise answers

    “AI beat professionals,” “a game was solved,” and “this program computes a strategy” are three different claims. The research becomes easier to navigate when you keep the exact game and the kind of evidence beside each result.

    For each paper, write the number of players, betting structure, objective and evaluation method. A two-player zero-sum model, a six-player chip game and a tournament with payouts are not interchangeable. A result about one does not automatically become a result about the others. Begin with the abstract and the definition of the task. When the prerequisites are unfamiliar, use the introductory CFR teaching material or the books and courses guide . You do not need to implement an algorithm before understanding what its claim is limited to.

    The 2007 CFR paper introduces counterfactual regret as a way to work with large imperfect-information games. The 2009 Monte Carlo CFR paper develops sampling variants and explains expected-update and regret properties. These are useful starting points for understanding why repeatedly updating strategies can be more than an arbitrary heuristic. The word “sampling” does not mean every sampled run has reached a strong strategy. To assess a concrete run, you still need its game definition, implementation, stopping criterion and evidence. A method's convergence statement is not the same as a finite-run guarantee for an unexamined program.

    Different poker-research milestones, different claims Research Scope to retain Do not conclude Cepheus The Alberta publication archive describes heads-up limit hold'em as essentially weakly solved. That all no-limit or tournament poker is solved. Libratus The authors' IJCAI record describes architecture and reported performance in heads-up no-limit hold'em. That its result covers six-player tournament payouts. DeepStack The original paper concerns deep reasoning in heads-up no-limit poker. That any neural poker model has the same demonstrated performance. Pluribus CMU's research account describes six-player no-limit experiments and limited-lookahead search. That empirical strength proves every multiplayer strategy is an equilibrium or covers every payout structure. The sources below preserve these distinctions. The institutional Pluribus summary is an accessible account, not a substitute for the full paper and supplement when checking a technical claim. The Alberta archive contains many papers; its inclusion does not mean every one was re-read for this guide.

    A reported match result depends on the game, opponents, sample and evaluation procedure. AIVAT is linked because it studies variance reduction for evaluating agents in imperfect-information games. Reducing measurement noise is a different contribution from improving the playing strategy itself. When you see a win rate or error bar, ask what the observational unit is, how the experiment was designed and what assumptions enter the estimator. Do not read “statistically significant against these opponents” as “best possible against every opponent.” Those are different questions even when the reported experiment is sound.

    A hand evaluator tells you which legal hand wins. A game environment implements actions and state changes. A solver seeks a strategy under an objective. A training interface presents exercises against a reference. One component working does not validate the entire chain. OpenSpiel is a documented framework for research in games. The directory also links PokerKit , the Poker Hand History specification and a hand-history dataset . Read the specific game support, version, license and data provenance before using them. No repository or dataset is described here as independently executed or audited.

    Record the title, version, original publication link, exact game, main claim, evidence and one unresolved question. Separate the authors' claims from your inferences. A useful outcome is knowing which result does not apply to your problem. This is a public research-reading map. It does not publish private solver code, training data or unvalidated charts. Study and experimentation belong away from active play and must follow the relevant operator's rules.

    Public abstracts, institutional descriptions and documentation pages provide the entry points. This guide is not a proof audit or experimental reproduction. Prepared with AI assistance. Published October 8, 2026 . Worked examples are fictional, not Nolan's hands or results. Sources and review limits accompany each listing. Use study material before or after play, not as live assistance. The advanced essay Poker under uncertainty connects these research areas through worked probability, inference, variance and ICM models. Use its source notes and downloadable calculations to separate a reproducible number from an assumption about a real player.

    Poker math: the right number for the right question.

    Compare call prices, pure-bluff thresholds, minimum defense frequency and pot-limit raises with exact worked examples and a portable reference.

    Read matching section

    Searchable article text, without exercise answers

    Three percentages can describe the same bet and answer three different questions. This reference keeps the price of a call, the success rate of a bluff and a range-defense benchmark separate. Use this page as a lookup during study, then follow the worked guides when a step is unclear. The table is also available as a downloadable math reference ; the visible numbers and download are generated from the same exact fractions. Check your own after-play accounting in the study calculation desk . It shows formulas and assumptions, not action recommendations.

    Call threshold = extra call / final pot after that call. Include wagers already in front of the players. Do not add a bet twice, and do not count a side pot you cannot win. For a first bet B into a pot P, a full call makes the final pot P + 2B. A fictional river price The pot is 120 before an opponent bets 90. It now contains 210. A call adds 90, making 300. The break-even equity is 90 / 300 = 30% , not 90 / 210. This assumes heads-up play, no rake and no further betting; ties count according to the fraction of the pot received. At exactly 30% equity the call and fold have equal chip EV in that model. A real decision still needs a justified opponent range. On an earlier street, raw showdown equity does not automatically describe the value of calling through future action. Continue with the pot-odds workshop and the equity-realization explanation .

    Scope: heads-up first bets, no rake, no further betting and no side pots. The call column uses equity, including ties. The bluff column assumes a bluff always loses when called. These are break-even thresholds, not recommended actions or observed opponent frequencies. Pure-bluff threshold = risk / (risk + reward). In the 120-pot example, risking 90 to win 120 requires 90 / 210 = 42.86% folds to break even. That is different from the caller's 30% equity threshold. At higher fold rates the zero-equity bluff has positive chip EV under the stated assumptions.

    The complementary first-bet minimum defense frequency is P / (P + B). For the example, it is 120 / 210 = 57.14% . It is a simplified benchmark for the frequency with which a range continues against a zero-equity bluff. It does not say that every hand needs 57.14% equity, or that you must personally call at that rate in every game. Raises, later betting, multiway pots, payout effects and the opponent's actual strategy change the problem. Do not give every player in a multiway pot the same heads-up defense quota. GTO Wizard's mathematical-misconceptions article explains why the simplified labels need these boundaries.

    Using the same fictional 120 pot and 90 bet, a player with no wager already committed on this street would call 90 to make 300, then raise by up to 300. That makes a maximum 390 total wager for that player, not 300 or 480. This is the accounting calculation, not an instruction to physically make a two-motion raise. With chips already committed, separate the new chips from the total street wager. Short stacks or action-reopening questions need additional checks. The official Omaha explanation describes pot-limit betting; the rules guide explains where procedural rulings belong.

    Stack in BB = stack / current big blind. A 28,500 stack at a 1,000 big blind is 28.5 BB. State when the stack was measured. SPR = effective chips remaining / pot at the same decision. Heads-up, 450 effective chips behind a 150 pot gives SPR 3. It is a situation descriptor, not a promise that a particular hand should commit its stack. An out must improve you to a winner for the question you are answering. Completing a flush is not enough when the opponent can have a better hand or redraw. The flush-and-redraw lab checks that distinction. Do not turn a two-card probability into a one-street calling rule.

    These selections retain the directory's access labels, individual review dates and limitations. Public-page reading is not a product accuracy test. Prepared with AI assistance. Published October 8, 2026 . Worked examples are fictional, not Nolan's hands or results. This is educational material for before or after play, not live assistance. For the reasoning behind these formulas, read Poker under uncertainty . It connects exact card counts with Bayesian range updates, future responses and noisy results, and includes reproducible fictional calculations.

    On this site · Read a hand

    Read the preflop chart before trusting the colors.

    Check game, position, stack convention, action history and combo weights before using a preflop chart as a study reference.

    Read matching section

    Searchable article text, without exercise answers

    A colored square is the last step in reading a preflop chart, not the first. The important information is the game, seats, stacks and actions that produced it.

    Identify the format, number of players, positions, starting stacks, blinds and antes. In cash games, check the rake model. In tournaments, distinguish a chip-EV reference from one modeling payouts or bounties. “20 BB” does not tell you whether the table is heads-up or nine-handed, or whether the hand begins before or after forced bets. A chart can change its payout objective while still allowing only shove or fold. Separate the action tree from the objective before comparing its recommendation with a model that allows small raises. Next, reproduce the action sequence. An unopened button chart does not answer a button decision after a raise and a caller. A push/fold solution answers a restricted action problem; it does not establish that a small raise or limp is inferior in a game where those actions are available. GTO Wizard's Study Mode documentation shows selection by positions and actions. Use a provider's setup information to identify the spot rather than treating a screenshot as a complete model.

    In standard hold'em, the 13 by 13 matrix groups the 1,326 unordered two-card combinations into 169 hand classes. Before any known-card removal, a pocket pair has 6 suit combinations, a suited nonpair has 4, and an offsuit nonpair has 12. Unblocked hold'em hand classes and physical combinations Class type Classes Combos each Total Pocket pairs 13 6 78 Suited nonpairs 78 4 312 Offsuit nonpairs 78 12 936 Thirteen plus 78 plus 78 gives 169 classes, while 78 plus 312 plus 936 gives 1,326 combinations. Selecting one offsuit class can therefore represent three times as many combinations as selecting one suited class. Read the matrix's actual labels and legend rather than assuming every product places suits or colors identically. SplitSuit's range-reading guide connects matrices, written ranges and percentages.

    A fictional frequency, not a solved recommendation Suppose a teaching chart assigns AKs a 50% raise and 50% call frequency, uniformly across its four unblocked suit combinations. That contributes 2 weighted combinations to each action. It does not mean that a player must raise exactly twice in the next four times they receive AKs, or that half of every holding in their entire range should raise. When a range is conditioned on earlier actions or known cards, both weights and available combinations can change. Do not average cell percentages without considering their weights. Use the combinations workshop for blocker and weighted-range examples.

    Fictional mismatch: you recorded 20,000 chips before posting a 1,000 big blind and a 1,000 big blind ante. The record is 20 BB before posting, but 18,000 chips remain behind. A source asking for a pre-posting stack and a source asking for chips behind need different inputs. Do not subtract the forced bets twice. With several opponents, a single “effective stack” can conceal different caps on different pots. Preserve the relevant players' stacks, positions and contributions. A two-player chart does not become a multiway answer by entering the smallest number at the table. The short-stack guide supplies the input checklist.

    Once the spot matches, compare the available actions and their expected values. A colored preference without EVs does not reveal whether alternatives are nearly tied or substantially different. A small displayed difference may also be smaller than the uncertainty created by your assumed ranges or approximate model. Make one controlled comparison: same positions and objective, but a different opening size or clearly documented range assumption. Label it as a model comparison, not a measurement of how opponents actually play. An exploitative adjustment needs a defensible read; a result alone is not that read. Save the source, version or access date, full inputs, and the question answered. Do not redistribute a provider's paid charts. This page teaches chart literacy; it does not publish validated opening or push/fold ranges.

    On this site · Live tournament preparation

    Poker rules and fair play: find the right authority.

    Find live and online rule sources, understand minimum raises and software restrictions, and report concerns without unsupported accusations.

    Read matching section

    Searchable article text, without exercise answers

    A tournament rulebook, an online software policy and advice in a forum answer different questions. Start with the authority for the game you are actually playing. For regulator lookups, account messages and complaint records, use the player-protection guide .

    Which source answers which question? Your question Start here A live tournament procedure The event's rules and tournament staff; a TDA reference where adopted. Cash-game betting, fees or seating The room's posted house rules and floor staff. An online tool, HUD or chart The exact operator's current software and game-integrity policy. A disputed online hand The operator's support or integrity channel, with the hand reference. A claim in a strategy discussion The original explanation and its assumptions, not an implied official ruling. At our October 16, 2026 check, the official TDA page displayed 2026 Rules, Version 1.1, September 21, 2026. Its floor-decision rule emphasizes fairness and final staff decisions. Do not assume a tournament rulebook is automatically the governing cash-game policy. TDA's download page links long and short formats and a route to translations; check each document's own version.

    Before acting, ask for the amount or the action to be clarified. TDA Rule 3 warns that action terms used in questions can be interpreted as a declaration. Neutral questions reduce avoidable ambiguity. For a dispute, ask for the floor and describe the sequence, amounts and statements without deciding the penalty yourself. Preserve the distinction between a rules question and strategic advice. A dealer can clarify an amount; another person should not choose your action. Keep filming, note-taking and devices within the event's actual restrictions.

    Fictional no-limit sequence A bets 100 and B raises to 250, an increment of 150. The next full raise is to 400 . If C instead goes all-in for 340, the 90 increase does not reopen B’s raising option in this sequence. The example illustrates the full-raise and reopening distinction in TDA Rules 45 and 49. Players who have not acted, cumulative short all-ins and limit games require their own checks. Read the applicable examples or ask the floor instead of extending this one sequence into a universal shortcut.

    PokerStars' third-party-tools policy distinguishes tools permitted generally, tools prohibited always, and tools restricted while its software is open. That last category is not limited to the seconds when a player faces a decision. A tool's marketing claim that it is compliant is not the operator's approval. GGPoker's Security & Ecology Policy is a separate operator document with its own treatment of external assistance, software and player conduct. Do not transfer a permission from one room to another, or assume that a second device changes the rule. For this site, the intended use is before or after a playing session, away from the table. Close the playing client when its policy requires that separation. These links are policy references, not endorsements, location-eligibility checks or permission to use this site's search during play.

    Keep the event or table identifier, time, relevant hand reference and a factual description. Separate what you directly observed from what you inferred. Send concerns through the room's appropriate private channel rather than posting another player's identifying information, account data or unsupported accusations. Ask what information is needed and preserve your own relevant records without covert collection. Do not buy mined opponent histories or try to investigate by breaking the operator's rules yourself. For account-security problems, use the operator's authenticated support route, not a link from an unsolicited message.

    Ask the organizer ahead of time about seating, communication or other accommodations you need. TDA Rule 10 addresses accommodations where possible; it is not a guarantee that a particular event has the arrangements you require. Confirm the actual plan before traveling. For gambling-related distress or difficulty controlling play, the support directory offers a separate route. Help is not something to postpone until you have studied more or recovered a loss.

    On this site · Other poker games

    Omaha hi-lo: play for a share, not just a low.

    Work through legal hand selection, quartering, counterfeiting and pot-share equity with complete fictional examples.

    Read matching section

    Searchable article text, without exercise answers

    Making a qualifying low answers only the first question. Can it win the low half outright? Can another player tie it? Can the same holding win high? This workshop separates those questions before attaching a percentage to a decision.

    In standard four-card Omaha hi-lo, use exactly two hole cards and three board cards for each five-card hand. The high and low selections may differ. A qualifying low has five distinct ranks of eight or lower, with the ace low; straights and flushes do not spoil the low. When nobody qualifies, the high winner takes the whole pot. The official rules describe these requirements. Before comparing players, write their best high and best qualifying low separately. Three low cards on the board are not enough if their ranks repeat. A board containing 2-2-7-K-Q provides only two distinct low ranks. No choice of two hole cards can turn it into five different low ranks.

    Fictional allocation: a 240-chip pot is split equally into high and low. Player A wins high outright; A and B tie for the best low. A receives 120 + 60 = 180 , while B receives 60 . The 60 is one quarter of the whole pot, not half. First identify eligibility for each pot if someone is all-in for less. Now suppose each player contributed 120 to this heads-up pot. B receives 60 but has a net result of -60. Being awarded some chips is not the same as profiting. Conversely, quartering does not automatically make every individual call wrong: a hypothetical guaranteed quarter of a 200-chip final pot is worth 50; paying an additional 40 for it has incremental chip EV of +10. That artificial calculation assumes no further action, no rake and certainty about the share. Do not carry the word “guaranteed” into a real hand where another holding, a side pot or an unknown card can change the award. The example distinguishes an entire hand's result from a decision made after earlier contributions are already spent.

    Fictional board change, checked from the legal card combinations Board: 3 of clubs, 5 of diamonds, 7 of hearts, king of clubs, 2 of hearts. A holds ace of spades, 2 of spades, queen of diamonds, jack of diamonds. B holds ace of hearts, 4 of hearts, queen of hearts, jack of spades. On the 3-5-7 flop, A can make 7-5-3-2-A , better than B's 7-5-4-3-A . After the river 2, A can still use the original three flop cards for the same seven-low. B can instead use A-4 with board 2-3-5 to make 5-4-3-2-A . A's low still qualifies, but B now beats it. As a separate version of the example, replace A's queen with the 4 of clubs. That extra low card gives A an alternative pair of hole cards, A-4, allowing the same wheel as B on this river. This is counterfeit protection in this example, not a promise that an extra low card protects every board or wins high.

    For a closed-action calculation, combine possible awards. A deliberately simplified model with a 20% chance of scooping, 40% chance of half, 20% chance of a quarter and 20% chance of nothing has expected pot share 0.20 + 0.40/2 + 0.20/4 = 45% . The probabilities sum to one. They are invented teaching inputs, not measured Omaha frequencies. Do not calculate high and low as independent events by default. The same board and cards determine both. A hand can share low while making a strong high, or miss both simultaneously. Future betting also means showdown share alone may not price the entire decision. Start with the math reference , then inspect the actual award conditions.

    Record the full board with suits, each known hole card, action amounts and pot eligibility. Enumerate the legal two-plus-three selections for high and low. Mark unknown opponents as ranges rather than inventing their holdings. Ask which runouts alter the best low, which improve high, and which merely make the hand look stronger without increasing its expected share. For a new player, getting the award right is a better first task than buying a chart and memorizing colors. Use the mixed-game overview to choose the correct rules before moving to a different variant. This workshop is not an opening-range recommendation.

    On this site · Other poker games

    Stud and lowball: change the rules before the strategy.

    Compare Stud8, razz, deuce-to-seven and Badugi, with worked hand comparisons and a rotation checklist.

    Read matching section

    Searchable article text, without exercise answers

    A wheel can be the best low in one game and a straight you do not want in another. Learn which hand wins, how it is constructed, and who acts first before borrowing a strategy from hold'em or the previous round of a mixed game.

    Core distinctions in the linked standard rule sets Game Hand selection Low rule Stud hi-lo eight-or-better Best five of your seven for each half Five distinct ranks, eight or lower; ace low Razz Best five of your seven Ace-to-five, no eight-or-better qualifier 2-7 triple draw Five-card draw hand Aces high; straights and flushes count against you Badugi Largest subset with distinct ranks and suits Four-card lowball; ace low The Stud8 , razz and 2-7 rule pages and Pagat's Badugi rules explain each system. They are references for the described variants, not evidence that a nearby room offers them today.

    Fictional comparison: under ace-to-five rules, 7-6-4-2-A loses to 7-5-4-3-2. Both are seven-lows, so compare their next highest cards: the five is lower than the six. Having an ace does not automatically make the first hand better. Do not add the card ranks and compare totals. In razz, a nine-low can win. The absence of an eight-low does not cancel the low contest because razz has no qualifier. In Stud8, a nine-low does not qualify for the low half. If nobody has a qualifying low there, the high winner takes the full pot. The ace-to-five wheel A-2-3-4-5 is a best low even when suited. In 2-7, aces are high, and straights and flushes are penalties. A non-flush 7-5-4-3-2 is the standard best 2-7 hand. The similar-looking 7-6-5-4-3 is a straight, not an improved seven-low. These are different ranking rules, not exceptions to memorize without context.

    Fictional hand: ace of clubs, 2 of diamonds, 3 of hearts, king of spades forms a four-card king-high Badugi. Ace of clubs, 2 of diamonds, 3 of hearts, 4 of hearts contains two hearts, so only three cards can be used together. The best three-card subset is A-2-3. The four-card king-high hand beats that three-card hand, despite its high king. Paired ranks create a similar selection problem. The process is to maximize the number of legal cards, then compare ranks among equal-sized subsets. A card that looks low may not add to the playable hand if its suit or rank clashes with a card already used.

    In stud variants, exposed cards affect what remains possible in the unseen deck. A hand note that records only your final seven cards misses information available during play. Write down relevant exposed cards you actually remember, the street and the action. Do not reconstruct opponents' earlier boards from their final showdown cards as though you remembered them then. Position is also not a fixed button advantage in the same way as hold'em. The razz procedure assigns the bring-in from the highest exposed third-street card, then starts later streets with the lowest exposed hand. A different stud game can use different criteria. Confirm the current rule before an unfamiliar forced action.

    Before each change of game, identify the hand-ranking system, the hole-card or subset requirement, the forced bets and action order, and the betting structure. For example, a displayed fixed-limit amount may name the small and big bet sizes rather than the blinds. A pot-limit hand uses a different raise calculation from a fixed-limit hand. A useful first practice task is to write two hands and explain which wins under two different games. Then vary one suit or rank and repeat. No wager is needed. The Omaha hi-lo workshop continues the split-pot comparison; the rules guide identifies where a live procedural question belongs.

    On this site · Read a hand

    Multiway pots: count the opponents and the pots.

    Distinguish a better call price from a better hand, separate pot eligibility and avoid importing heads-up defense quotas.

    Read matching section

    Searchable article text, without exercise answers

    Another caller adds money to the pot and another hand you must beat. Those changes happen together. A cheaper-looking call is not proof that the decision has become more profitable.

    Fictional river: 90 chips are in the pot. A bets 30, B calls 30, and C closes the action by calling 30. With no rake or side pots, the final pot is 180 . C's additional call is 30, so its break-even expected pot share is 30 / 180 = 16.67% . If B had folded instead, the final pot after C's call would be 150 and the threshold 20%. The lower threshold does not answer whether C's hand reaches it. B's call is new information about a competing range. Compare the hand against both ranges and the actual distribution of possible awards, including ties. Counting the money is exact; assigning those ranges is an assumption.

    If C has not acted and you are deciding in B's seat, the final pot is not known yet. C could fold, call or raise. Treating C's future call as guaranteed understates what can happen next. Write the current action order alongside the price rather than only recording an attractive fraction. On an earlier street, opponents may bet again even after everyone calls now. An equity calculator that assumes a free showdown does not automatically value that future decision tree. GTO Wizard's original multiway discussion is useful context for closing action and shared defense, but its heuristics are not mandatory frequencies for an unknown table.

    Fictional all-ins: A contributes 50, B contributes 200 and C contributes 200. There are no other contributions or deductions. The main pot is 3 × 50 = 150 . The side pot is 2 × 150 = 300 . A can win the 150 main pot; only B and C can win the side pot. The two awards total 450. A's chance of having the best hand against everyone is not the only calculation B needs. B could lose the main pot to A and still beat C for the larger side pot. Evaluate each eligible pot against the players contesting it, then add expected awards. The side-pot lab shows refunds, eligibility and chip conservation in more detail.

    When one player is all-in and the remaining players have not put additional unmatched-by-the-all-in-player chips into a separate pot, that side pot is dry. It contains zero. A bet may make another live player fold, but the all-in player remains eligible for the main pot and cannot be bluffed out of it. That observation is not a universal instruction to check. A bet can have value, protection or other effects. It does mean that “I can win everything by making the other player fold” is wrong while the all-in player still contests the main pot. Keep the pot you are trying to win explicit.

    A pure bluff into two opponents must get the required combination of folds. The relevant event is both players folding, not either player's individual fold rate. In a deliberately artificial independent model, two 50% fold rates yield 0.50 × 0.50 = 25% joint folds, not 50%. In actual sequential action, use conditional probabilities: P(A folds) multiplied by P(B folds given A folded). The second player's response can change after seeing the first action, and card removal links their possible hands. Assuming independence without checking it creates false precision. A heads-up minimum-defense number is not a quota to impose on every player in a multiway pot.

    Write the action order, relevant stacks, contributions, pot eligibility and possible further actions. Separate a made hand from its ability to improve to the best hand; a draw can complete and still lose. State which range changes would reverse the conclusion. Use the study calculation desk only for its stated accounting tasks, not as a multiway solver. For the playing decisions around this accounting, read limped and multiway live pots . It connects isolation raises, hand quality and a counted cash-game hand with separate tournament considerations. For study, change one input at a time. Move the caller to a seat that closes action, remove a side pot or alter a stated range. Explain which conclusion changes and why. This creates a checkable lesson without pretending one fictional example gives a universal strategy.

    On this site · Learning resources

    Turn a poker video or podcast into one useful lesson.

    Use annotated media starting points, distinguish transcripts from show notes and build a short study record without copying copyrighted material.

    Read matching section

    Searchable article text, without exercise answers

    Watching more poker is not the same as answering a poker question. Choose one thing to learn, find a source that exposes enough information, and leave with a small record you can check.

    A hand breakdown can help reconstruct action. A lecture can develop an argument. An interview may explain a player's experience without supplying a complete strategic proof. All can be worthwhile, but they should not be judged as though they perform the same task. For a calculation, prefer material with written inputs, readable graphics or a usable transcript. For a conversation about playing recreationally, a clear episode description can help you choose what to hear, but it does not establish what every guest said. Keep the difference between selecting a programme and reviewing its contents visible.

    Combinations: MIT's Lecture 7 with Will Ma is presented as an in-depth hand-analysis session. Its page includes a transcript interface and an authorized offline-video route. The page was inspected; the complete video and transcript were not reviewed for this listing. Use the combinations workshop as an independent exercise rather than assuming the lecture endorses its examples. Tournament models: MIT's Lecture 6 is described as covering chip values and tournament equity, with a transcript interface and linked slides. It is a 2016 course, not current software documentation. Try writing the model's inputs before opening an ICM tool. The page and available formats were inspected, not the full lecture. Recreational goals: Thinking Poker episode 466 introduces a conversation with RecPoker participants about recreational players. Audio and show notes are provided; no full transcript was verified. Its topic is a reason to consider listening, not a claim that this site has listened to and validated the whole episode. A written interview: the James “SplitSuit” Sweeney interview page includes substantial transcript text. This offers a text-first route into a creator conversation. Interview statements remain personal views rather than independently tested performance claims.

    For a hand video, pause at one decision. Write the position, stack, pot, action and cards that the player could know then. Keep later-revealed hole cards in a separate line. A broadcast graphic can give the audience information the player did not possess. Fictional viewing task: the pot is 80, an opponent bets 40, and a call would end the betting. Write the 40 / 160 = 25% threshold before the reveal, then identify the range assumption needed to compare your hand with it. If the video does not supply enough information, the correct note may be “range unknown,” not a confident verdict.

    Search within available text for the topic, then read the surrounding explanation. A transcript label does not guarantee that every card, suit or bet amount has been captured accurately. Cross-check technical numbers against the video or slides where available. When that is not possible, label the uncertainty rather than silently correcting it from memory. Save a link and a timestamp or heading in your private note. Use your own words for the takeaway. Do not redistribute a full transcript, video, paywalled chart or course download merely because you can access it. Link to the publisher's authorized resource instead.

    A complete session might end with one reconstructed pot, one hand-ranking correction, or one disagreement whose assumptions you can name. It does not need another hour of viewing. Compare the takeaway with a second suitable source only when that comparison serves the original question. The answer finder can collect up to 12 public entries into a downloadable study list. The list stores links and catalogue context, not a copy of the underlying media or your search terms. The resource-check sheet provides space for your own question and unresolved points.

    Check the room, the rules and your protections.

    Find regulator and operator information, protect account access, preserve complaint records and reach support without gambling-site rankings.

    Read matching section

    Searchable article text, without exercise answers

    A familiar brand, polished application or working payment screen does not answer every question about access, permissions and player protection. Start with the exact operator and jurisdiction rather than an affiliate ranking.

    Record the jurisdiction where you intend to participate, the operator's legal name, exact website domain and the product you are checking. A casino approval, a software-supplier entry and a poker offering are not interchangeable labels. This page is a source-finding checklist, not legal advice or a worldwide list of places where you may play. For Great Britain , the Gambling Commission business register supports lookup by business, trading name, domain or account number. Inspect status and licensed activities, not simply the existence of a name. The register itself cautions that domain and trading-name data are supplied by businesses and are not guaranteed accurate. No operator-specific licence check was performed for this guide. For New Jersey , the Division of Gaming Enforcement information page points to authorized sites, permit holders and dispute information. Its current search-index text was inspected; direct retrieval was blocked. Follow the regulator's own links and check the current record yourself before relying on it. No provider list is reproduced here. These two examples do not establish eligibility elsewhere or resolve your individual circumstances. When the relevant record cannot be confirmed, leave the answer unresolved. Do not use location masking, false identity information or another person's account to work around restrictions.

    Find the applicable age, identity, location and account requirements, how verification is completed, and how to contact support through an authenticated route. Check withdrawal conditions, fees, bonus restrictions and account-closure information. Keep a dated private copy of the terms that matter to your decision. An unfamiliar condition is a reason to pause, not to assume a promotional summary overrules it. Separate permissions for playing from permissions for software and assistance. An operator can restrict a tool even between hands or while its client is open. Use the rules and fair-play guide for that distinct question. This website's study tools are intended for use away from play, not to decide an active hand.

    The FTC's phishing guidance recommends contacting a company through a website or number known to be genuine rather than links or details supplied in a suspicious message. Keep software updated and use multi-factor authentication where offered. A copied logo is not proof of identity. Fictional example: a message claims that your poker account will be frozen unless you immediately enter a one-time code on a linked page. Do not follow the link or send the code to the sender. Open the independently verified operator site or application and check through its authenticated support route. Keep sensitive records out of a public forum or this site's contact form.

    Keep the account or event reference, date and time, the relevant transaction or hand identifier, your factual description, and the support case number. Separate the remedy you request from speculation about motives. Preserve the original correspondence rather than editing screenshots to make the case sound stronger. Find the operator's complaint procedure and then the applicable independent or regulatory route. New Jersey's DGE information specifies an operator-first process for Internet disputes and asks for the original complaint and response. That is a New Jersey process, not a universal deadline or promise of recovery. Check the current instructions and obtain qualified advice when a legal dispute requires it.

    Look for the operator's limit, time-out, closure and self-exclusion information without treating any one setting as a guarantee against harm. There is no need to recover a loss before seeking support. The National Council on Problem Gambling connects people in the United States with support and state resources. The directory also includes GamCare for its stated service area. For a live visit, ask staff in advance about seating, communication and other accommodations you need. Record the arrangement actually confirmed, including who to contact on arrival. A general accessibility statement is not proof that a particular event can meet a particular need. The event planner keeps these questions beside your time and travel plan.
